Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

noise noun

also noises, a noise, din, racket, clatter, make a noise, raise a racket, make a racket, raise a rumpus, ruckus, why are you raising such a ruckus?, rumpus

classical

Liv. 5.47.3: ad nocturnōs strepitūs
Caes. B.G. 2.11: magnō cum strepitū ac tumultū
Traupman 276, 368

strepitus, strepitūs m.

noun, fourth declension

noise, din, clatter

Any loud, confused noise: of wheels, doors, rivers, a crowd, the city (Lewis & Short). To make a noise is strepere (see noisy).

Other words

  • sonitus, sonitūs m. — a sound, a noise

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 7.60: remōrum (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 8.596

    A sound of any kind, of hooves, oars, wind or thunder, not necessarily unpleasant; strepitus is noise as din.

  • clāmor, clāmōris m. — shouting, the noise of voices

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 56.1: varius clāmor

    A shout or outcry, and the noise of many voices together.

  • crepitus, crepitūs m. — a rattle, a clatter, a creak

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Liv. 5.47.4: ālārumque crepitū

    A sharp, short noise: the flapping of wings, the creak of a door, the crackle of fire.

  • clāmōrem tollere — raise a shout, make a racket

    phrase: tollō, tollere, sustulī, sublātum · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.79: quō aspectū exterrita clāmōrem sustulit (Lewis & Short s.v. exterreō); Traupman 106: to raise a racket, clāmōrem tollere; Traupman 107: why are you raising such a ruckus?, quid istum clāmōrem tollis (pl. tollitis)?

  • turbās dare — raise a rumpus, make trouble

    also used · modern · Traupman 106: raise a rumpus, turbās dare

    Traupman’s phrase; neither Lewis & Short nor the loci collections quote it. Turba in comedy is an uproar or a fuss.

Examples

  • tantō silentiō in summum ēvāsēre ut nōn custōdēs sōlum fallerent, sed nē canēs quidem, sollicitum animal ad nocturnōs strepitūs, excitārent

    they reached the top so quietly that they not only slipped past the guards but did not even wake the dogs, creatures that fret at every noise in the nightLiv. 5.47.3

  • ecce undique mē varius clāmor circumsonat: suprā ipsum balneum habitō

    listen: noise of every kind surrounds me; I live right above a bath-houseSen. Ep. 56.1

  • Quid istum clāmōrem tollis?

    Why are you raising such a ruckus?Traupman 107

  • Quid istum clāmōrem tollis (tollitis)?

    Why are you raising such a ruckus?Traupman 372

See also noisy, loud, silence, crash, quiet!.
